audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields called Lightning Rush a dash and a gap-closer ('dashes him straight into beam range', 'dash back out', 'his only gap-closer').
audit.why: Riot's text: Kennen 'morphs into a lightning form, enabling him to pass through units', gaining Move Speed on entry and attack speed on exit. It is a movement-speed form with unit-collision immunity — no dash flag in the kit. That changes the counterplay completely: it cannot hop a wall, and it cannot yank him out of the nest instantly, so once he is inside the beams at 10s cooldown he has to WALK out through them.
audit.corrected: Restated as a 10s speed form in whys[2], early, wants.foe[0], spikes[1], report[5] and dosFull[0].d, with the wall point stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere; 'respect his ult timer' with no timer given.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom is a FLAT 120s at every rank — it never gets shorter, so one burned ultimate hands Heimerdinger a two-minute window against an 11s grenade. Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6s, Thundering Shuriken 7s down to 4s, Electrical Surge 13s down to 6s.
audit.corrected: 120s flat written into breakdown.cooldowns and mid; the 10s form and 11s grenade written into the trading and spike text.

audit.why: Full and content charts agree row-for-row (Heim, Skill, Kennen, Kennen, Heim, Kennen, Kennen) and the whys argue the flips: your nest owns 1-3, his 6 is the swing, and the poke war after that is a wash at a 51.3% win rate. Packet.levelChart differs at rows 2, 4 and 6 but the prose reasoning is the stronger read and the two layers are already consistent, so no chart edits proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization named Mercury's Treads but never said why MR over armour.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags onhit-itemization: Electrical Surge applies on-hit and scales with his attack speed, and the whole kit is magic damage. Armour reads this trade wrong.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown late-game text and report[8].

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Lightning Rushes' (wants.you[1]) and 'Land Slicing Maelstrom' (wants.foe[2]) as probable wrong names. Both are FALSE POSITIVES — the first is the real name inflected as a verb, the second is the real name preceded by 'Land'. No name edits made on that basis.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape. E-stun when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: a flat 120s at every rank — that is the only cooldown that kills you. - Lightning Rush: 10s at rank 1, and it is a speed form, not a dash. - UPGRADE!!!: 100s, kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Kennen's Lightning Rush: His escape. E-stun when it’s down. When it is down — E-stun + turret him.
edits.after: Lightning Rush is a speed form, not a dash — it cannot cross walls. E-stun him inside the nest and he stays.

edits.before: His escape. E-stun when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: A 10s speed form, not a dash — no wall-hop. Engage once it is down or spent.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Three Marks of the Storm stun you; break contact at two stacks.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Liandry's Torment  (turret burn), then Rylai's Crystal Scepter; boots Mercury's Treads.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Liandry's Torment, then Rylai's; boots Mercury's Treads — MR beats armour, his W is magic on-hit.

edits.before: Your nest zones his step-ups and his only gap-closer, Lightning Rush, dashes him straight into beam-and-stun range — his commits are suicidal here.
edits.after: Your nest zones his step-ups and Lightning Rush is a 10s speed form, not a dash — it walks him into beam-and-stun range and cannot hop a wall out.

edits.before: Lightning Rush in, land the W (Electrical Surge) and Q-shuriken poke, and dash back out before your E grenade or beams connect
edits.after: Lightning Rush in, land Electrical Surge and a Thundering Shuriken, and run back out on the speed before your grenade connects

edits.before: With two turrets banked plus E (CH-3X Lightning Grenade), any Lightning Rush in for a W-Q poke combo can be met with a center-stun and double beams — your best window to punish him for stepping into the nest.
edits.after: With two turrets banked plus E (CH-3X Lightning Grenade), any Lightning Rush in for a W-Q poke combo can be met with a center-stun and double beams — the form is 10s, so he cannot get back out and it hops no walls.

edits.before: Kennen pokes from outside beam range with his Q shuriken, but the lane is yours to dictate early: slam a turret on the wave and he has to walk into the nest to last-hit, eating chip and a beam every time. Don't chase his poke — bank your Q charges, watch his Mark of the Storm stacks so he never lands a free passive stun, and hold E (CH-3X Lightning Grenade) for the moment he Lightning Rushes in. If he dashes into the nest to trade, that's your opening: he's inside the beams and his only escape is on cooldown.
edits.after: Kennen pokes from outside beam range with Thundering Shuriken, but the lane is yours to dictate early: slam a turret on the wave and he has to walk into the nest to last-hit, eating chip and a beam every time. Don't chase his poke — bank your Q charges, watch his Mark of the Storm stacks so he never lands a free passive stun, and hold E (CH-3X Lightning Grenade) for the moment he Lightning Rushes in. If he Rushes into the nest to trade, that's your opening: it is a speed form, not a dash, so at 10s down he has to walk out through the beams.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your strongest stretch — with two turrets banked plus your center-stun, any Lightning Rush dive in for a W-Q combo can be punished with a CH-3X stun and double beams, so make him pay for every step into range. But level 6 swings the math to Kennen: Slicing Maelstrom dropped on top of you stacks Mark of the Storm and stun-locks an immobile, dashless yordle, and his Q-W-R burst plus any gank kills you through the buildings. Respect his ult timer harder than he respects your grenade — never sit on low HP inside R-flash range.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are your strongest stretch — with two turrets banked plus your center-stun, any Lightning Rush dive in for a W-Q combo can be punished with a CH-3X stun and double beams, so make him pay for every step into range. But level 6 swings the math to Kennen: Slicing Maelstrom dropped on top of you stacks Mark of the Storm and stun-locks an immobile, dashless yordle, and his Q-W-R burst plus any gank kills you through the buildings. Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank — count it from the moment he burns it, and until it returns your 11s grenade owns every step-up he takes.

edits.before: This stays a poke war and it stays even. With Liandry's and banked turret beams you out-sustain his shuriken-and-rocket chip and own any side lane you've already zoned, but Kennen scales into a teamfight Slicing Maelstrom that ignores your immobility entirely. Build MR and Mercury's Treads so his combo can't one-shot you, cash your sieging edge in skirmishes before fights get chaotic, and never facecheck — one clean point-blank R angle on you and the fight is his.
edits.after: This stays a poke war and it stays even. With Liandry's and banked turret beams you out-sustain his shuriken-and-rocket chip and own any side lane you've already zoned, but Kennen scales into a teamfight Slicing Maelstrom that ignores your immobility entirely. Build MR and Mercury's Treads — Electrical Surge applies on-hit and scales with his attack speed, so armour reads the trade wrong — and never facecheck: one clean point-blank R angle and the fight is his.

notes: Main find: Lightning Rush is NOT a dash. Riot's text describes a lightning form with unit-collision immunity and bonus Move Speed; the kit carries no dash flag. Six fields sold it as a gap-closer/dash, which mistrains the reader into thinking he can instantly leave the nest and hop walls. Corrected. Slicing Maelstrom's flat 120s (never scales down) is the single most useful number in this matchup and was absent. Both packet suspectNames are false positives.
